---
title: "Stan vs. Randy"
subtitle: "TWO CHARACTER DIALOGUE TRENDS"
format: html
---

This comparison uses recorded transcript lines from seasons 1-21. Each character's line count is shown as a share of all transcript lines in that season.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(southparkr)
library(plotly)

dialogue_lines <- episode_lines |>
  mutate(character = str_remove_all(character, "[:\"]"))

season_totals <- dialogue_lines |>
  count(season_number, name = "all_lines")

seasons <- sort(unique(dialogue_lines$season_number))

stan_randy <- dialogue_lines |>
  filter(character %in% c("Stan", "Randy")) |>
  count(season_number, character, name = "lines") |>
  complete(
    season_number = seasons,
    character = c("Stan", "Randy"),
    fill = list(lines = 0)
  ) |>
  left_join(season_totals, by = "season_number") |>
  mutate(
    share = 100 * lines / all_lines,
    character = recode(character, Stan = "Stan Marsh", Randy = "Randy Marsh")
  )

stan_randy_plot <- stan_randy |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = season_number,
    y = share,
    color = character,
    group = character,
    text = paste(
      "Season:", season_number,
      "<br>Character:", character,
      "<br>Transcript lines:", lines,
      "<br>Share of all lines:", round(share, 2), "%"
    )
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Randy Marsh" = "#005A9C", "Stan Marsh" = "#A33A13")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seasons) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Stan and Randy's dialogue share by season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Share of all transcript lines",
    color = "Character",
    caption = "Source: southparkr transcript data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(stan_randy_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
period_values <- stan_randy |>
  mutate(period = case_when(
    season_number <= 7 ~ "Early",
    season_number >= 15 ~ "Late",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(period)) |>
  group_by(period, character) |>
  summarise(mean_share = mean(share), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = character, values_from = mean_share)

knitr::kable(
  period_values,
  digits = 1,
  col.names = c("Period", "Randy Marsh", "Stan Marsh"),
  caption = "Average dialogue share in early and late seasons"
)
```

Randy's later-period share is compared with Stan's so the change is visible in one set of values. This is a dialogue measure, not a measure of screen time or narrative importance.
